ref_extractions.title: The Temple University Hospital EEG corpus
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the original TUEG corpus paper from 2013, which predates the TUH EEG Events corpus. The dataset 'tuh_eeg_events' was created later for specific event detection tasks with 6-way classification labels. This paper only introduces the general TUEG database without event-level annotations or the specific event classification task.

ref_extractions.title: Temple University EEG Corpus
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the general landing page for the TUH EEG Corpus access. It mentions TUSZ (seizure) and TUAR (artifact) corpora but does not mention 'tuh_eeg_events' specifically. There is no discussion of the 6-way event classification task (SPSW, PLED, GPED, ARTF, EYEM, BCKG) that defines the tuh_eeg_events dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Recent Advances in the TUH EEG Corpus: Improving the Interrater Agreement for Artifacts and Epileptiform Events
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper discusses TUSZ (seizure detection) and TUAR (artifact detection) corpora, which are related to event detection but are distinct from tuh_eeg_events. The paper mentions epileptiform events and artifacts, which overlap with some classes in tuh_eeg_events, but it focuses on interrater agreement improvements for TUSZ and TUAR rather than the specific 6-way classification task. The event types mentioned (seizures, artifacts, eye movements) suggest related annotation work but not the exact tuh_eeg_events dataset.

ref_extractions.title: The TUH EEG Corpus: A Big Data Resource for Automated EEG Interpretation
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper explicitly introduces the TUH EEG Corpus and defines a concrete 6-way classification task: (1) Spike and/or sharp waves, plus other event classes. The paper states 'we are focusing on a 6-way classification' and describes predicting 'commonly occurring events from simple features.' This matches the tuh_eeg_events dataset structure with event-based classification. The paper describes the pilot experiments on event detection from the raw EEG signal data using 3,762 sessions.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: 1 sec epochs, features computed every 0.1 secs using 0.2 sec analysis windows (from related 2015 paper); 6-way classification with closed-loop and open-set testing
ref_extractions.label_mapping: 6 classes: SPSW, PLED, GPED, ARTF, EYEM, BCKG
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Original foundational paper defining the event classification task on TUH EEG Corpus; 6-way classification explicitly defined
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Paper explicitly states 'we are focusing on a 6-way classification' and describes event detection from raw EEG signals with specific event classes matching tuh_eeg_events

ref_extractions.title: Improved EEG Event Classification Using Differential Energy
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper explicitly uses the TUH EEG Corpus for event classification and clearly defines the exact 6-way classification task with all six event classes: SPSW, PLED, GPED, ARTF, EYEM, and BCKG. The paper describes the AutoEEG system architecture with HMM-based recognition producing epoch labels. The epoch parameters are explicitly stated: 1 sec epochs, features computed every 0.1 secs using 0.2 sec analysis windows, with 10 frames of 0.1 secs per epoch for HMM modeling. This is the definitive paper for the tuh_eeg_events dataset task definition.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: 1 sec epochs; features computed every 0.1 sec using 0.2 sec analysis windows; 10 frames of 0.1 sec per epoch for HMM; 0.9 sec window for differential energy; deltas computed with N=9 (0.9 sec), delta-deltas with N=3
ref_extractions.label_mapping: 6 classes: SPSW, PLED, GPED, ARTF, EYEM, BCKG
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Definitive paper for tuh_eeg_events: explicitly defines all 6 event classes, epoching strategy, and HMM-based classification approach on TUH EEG Corpus
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Paper explicitly states 'The system detects three events of clinical interest: (1) spike and/or sharp waves (SPSW), (2) PLED, (3) GPED' and 'three events used to model background noise: (1) artifacts (ARTF), (2) eye movement (EYEM), (3) background (BCKG)' with exact epoch parameters

feasibility_reason: Two relevant papers explicitly describe a 6-way clinical EEG event classification task on this dataset, with clearly defined event classes: spike/sharp waves (SPSW), PLED, GPED, artifacts (ARTF), eye movement (EYEM), and background (BCKG). The event structure supports meaningful multi-class classification of pathological and normal EEG patterns.

event_annotations.notes: No events detected in the dataset. The evidence collection was unable to locate any EEG files, event markers, or sidecar files that would contain event ID mappings. The dataset structure (v2.0.1/edf/) contains eval/ and processed_train/ subdirectories, but repeated attempts to find EDF files within eval/000-099 directories failed. The AAREADME.txt file could not be parsed due to formatting issues (ParserError at line 51). The processed_train/ directory contains .pkl files (binary pickle format, unreadable as text) with naming pattern 'aaaaaaar_00000001-N.pkl', but no event information could be extracted. Without accessible events.tsv, events.json, or readable EEG headers containing event markers, no event annotations can be assigned.
